Inspection Date: 8/19/2024
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Nichols A (1H) well site located in Smithfield Township, Bradford County on 8/19/2024 at 1110 hours. The weather was 67 degrees F with cloudy skies. Rain fell onsite within the past 24 hours.This inspection was conducted to summarize site remediation efforts completed by Blackhill Energy after a release was reported to the DEP on 7/29/2024 and violations were cited in inspection report #3804993. Pad material/soils located within the excavation area today were field measured for electrical conductivity and ranged from 0.08 to 0.23mS/cm. No pooled fluids were located within the excavation area, however, pooled fluids on the pad surface near the excavation area were field measured for electrical conductivity and ranged from 155 to 275us/cm. No evidence of any portion of the release remaining was observed today. On behalf of Blackhill Energy, Moody and Associates (Moody's) submitted a 15-day interim report and NOV (notice of violation) response to the DEP on 8/7/2024. The report is attached to this inspection via file and has been uploaded to eFACTS. The NOV response indicated that interim remedial actions and site characterization activities were initiated on 7/29/2024. The NOV response also indicated that impacted pad materials and soils with electrical conductivity readings above 1.0mS/cm were excavated and placed in a lined roll-off container. Moody's collected soil attainment samples for the PADEP brine list and Ethylene Glycol following the PADEP's systematic random sampling protocol. Due to the presence of foam released with the produced water, Ethylene Glycol was added to the analyte list. Blackhill Energy plans to submit a Statewide Health Standard Site Characterization and Final Report within 90 days.Violations cited on 7/29/2024 against API #015-21167 remain outstanding at this site from the previous release. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has been confirmed.I departed the site at 1215 hours.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8180429
Permit API: 125-22753
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/12/2024
Comments: On 03/12/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well site following violations issued on 12/19/2023 (IR 3662363, Enforcement 423308). I was accompanied by PA DEP Compliance Specialist, George Traister. Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) were issued on 12/19/2023. The violations were issued as outstanding on 01/31/2024 (IR 3704581).The following was observed on 03/12/2024:Conductivity readings were taken within the water and gravel in the tank battery. The valve on Tank 1 looked to be leaking fluid. Crystallization was noted on the valve (Photo 1). The water within the battery around Tank 1 did not display elevated readings (Photo 2). The fluid escaping from the valve is recommended to be addressed. A reading was obtained within the gravel around the pan of Tank 4. This reading was 4.28 mS (Photo 3).Readings were taken within the gravel in the battery around Tank 5 and within the fluid in the pan. The readings within the gravel were 4.76 mS and 4.26 mS (Photos 4, 5). The reading within the pan was 17.30 mS (Photos 6, 7), which may indicate fluids leaking from tank fluid removal or from the valve itself. I recommend that this is addressed. The piping on the drain from the battery has been shortened. The exterior end is capped, and no elevated conductivity was noted on the ground below. The interior end is open, and I recommend that this is also capped. The water level in the battery is close to the edge of the pipe (Photos 8, 9). Stabilization has been added to the earthen berm. I recommend that additional is added as needed (Photos 10, 11).Pans are under each tank valve (Photo 12).Wet spots were noted on the exterior of the earthen berm. Conductivity readings were taken within these noted areas and resulted in the following: 4.00 mS, 6.33 mS, 5.44 mS. Another reading resulted in 1.15 mS. I recommend that fluid from inside the battery is not migrate through the berm. Livestock activity in the vicinity is taken into consideration (Photos 13-17). The violations issued on 12/29/2023 and 01/31/2024 remain outstanding.

Comments: On 3/12/2024 OGI Geoffrey Lutty conducted an onsite inspection of the John B Kline 2, API 129-26164. The well was surrounded by overgrown vegetation. The well and equipment displayed moderate corrosion. The production tank was not connected. It is recommended to remove any unused equipment under OGA3216(c). No tag was posted with operator information in accordance with OGA3211(g). No gas leaks, spill, or signs of incidents were observed while onsite. No APR has been submitted for the 2023 year. A 2022 APR is on file which indicates production. No MIA has been submitted for the 2023 year. A 2022 MIA is on file. The department requests the operator verify if the well is currently producing. Comments: Inspection conducted in response to a spill notification received yesterday 2/26/19 about a release of an estimated 10 gallons of produced water that had occurred at 1730 the same day. He explained that an 18-wheeler off-loading produced water from a battery of frac tanks had inadvertently pumped produced water out of the truck into the tank instead of pumping it out of the tank and into the truck. This activated a pressure relief valve on the truck which led to the release of the produced water. Mr. Deming said that a vacuum truck on site immediately sucked up the fluid and gravel from the pad surface was scraped with a skid steer and placed into a container for disposal. At the time of this inspection, the site was snow-covered and the impacted gravel material had already been removed. During the inspection, a zipper frac was in process on the 10H and 5H wells. The site was in good shape overall. The secondary containment appeared to be fully intact with no visible damage. Fresh water was being pumped in from a FWI as well as trucked in to the site. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Comments: On 10/6/20 at 0955 hrs., I conducted an inspection of PA General Energy Co., LLC's J Elmer Lockhart 1127 well (API 063-32044) in Grant Twp., Indiana Co. in response to a reported release of brine/production fluid from a vent at the well head. The well was shut-in by the operator on 10/1/20, prior to the release. A well tag is affixed to the well head. A site ID sign with the operator's name, address, phone number, and well permit should be posted pursuant to OGA 3211(G). On 10/5/20, the operator reported a release of brine/production fluid from a vent between casing strings to the Department. The exact amount of fluid released is unknown, but it was initially estimated as a couple of barrels. Upon inspection of the release area, the size of the impacted area appears to be consistent with a multi-barrel release. The fluid impacted an area at the well head, then flowed down an access road to a lower area where the landowner has various junk vehicles staged. At the time of inspection, Huey Brothers had excavated the lower area and access road. Moody & Associates has been contracted as a consultant and was field screening for soil conductivity. PID screening was yielding no readings. On 10/7/20 I received an update from Nathan Harris with PGE stating that the excavation of the lower area was reaching depths of 10-12 feet in spots, due to the released material hitting an area of weathered rock and migrating vertically.The release of production fluid/brine from the well head constitutes violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1), and CSL 402(b). The violations associated with this release will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release and demonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.

Report Details

Unconventional: No

Comments: This conventional well is equipped with rods and tubing. The pump jack has been removed from the well, the annulus of the well remains connected to a gathering line. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. The well is not equipped with a well tag, nor is there a site ID sign posted at the location.A tank battery containing four steel tanks and two poly tanks inside of an earthen containment is located approximately 200 feet east of this well. There are indications that production fluids (primarily brine) have repeatedly been released onto the gravel inside of this containment. The soil is stained and specific conductance of the soil is elevated at the western edge where fluid from the tanks appears to have been released, and at the eastern edge of the containment where fluids appear to have been released from a pipeline riser/blow off).Vegetation is absent and deer tracks are very dense on the surface outside of the west/northwest extent of the containment, as it appears the released fluids have migrated through the earthen walls at the natural contour onto which the gravel and earthen wells were constructed. Stained soil and elevated specific conductance continue westward into a roadside ditch of Forest Road 219 until the ditch reaches a cross culvert approximately 300 feet away.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29931, 053-29930, 053-29944, 053-29955 and 053-29945 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. These E and S concerns are considered part of E and S violations that are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29816 (Warrant 2980 #45).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

Comments: On 9/10/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Gergely 1 well in Munster Township, Cambria County.This inspection was conducted in response to a referral from OGI Matt Woods (Inspection ID: 4268198 on 9/01/2026; Inspection ID: 4269845 on 9/03/2026). OGI Matt Woods requested that a WQS follow up because of potential surface pollution concerns regarding a plastic-lined pit observed during IR 4269845.This inspection is not evaluating compliance with Order 450586, as it is being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- No equipment related to production and/or well plugging operations was observed on site. The plastic-lined pit documented in IR 4269845 was not observed during this inspection (Photos 11 and 19). No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site at the time of inspection. No plugging monument was observed at the former location of the well. The API number and Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) were found on site (Photos 16 and 17).- The access road and well site remain heavily rutted, which appears to be caused by vehicles and machinery that were tracked-in for well plugging operations. Some mulch and seed was observed on site. However, the mulch and seed implemented on site is inadequate, as large portions of exposed soil are observable (Photos 12-15 and 20-21).- No perimeter Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls were observed on site. No E and S Restoration plan was observed on site during this inspection.Based on today's inspection, the violations issued in IR 4263564 against the heavy tire rutting and for failure to have the E and S/Restoration plan available on site will remain outstanding. An additional violation is being issued in this inspection for failure to implement adequate seed and temporary stabilization on areas that were disturbed by well plugging operations.The outstanding violations issued for failure to post the API number and operator's information on site are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.The Department requests that the Operator provide an electronic copy of the Control and Disposal Plan and provide clarification regarding the purpose of the plastic-lined pit observed during the time of IR 4269845, what it contained, and method of disposal used. Please provide this clarification no later than 9/29/2026. Additional violations may be forthcoming upon receipt and review of the clarification from the Operator.

Comments: On January 8, 2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation of Diversified's Dinunno 1 plugged well site located in Springhill Township, Fayette County. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 3/20/2025, therefore the well site should be fully restored by 12/20/2025 and a well site restoration report be submitted to the Department by 2/18/2026 or a well site restoration extension request should be submitted by 9/20/2025 (6 months after the plugging of the well). IR 4115541 documents the return of a 12/19/2025 submitted well site restoration extension request.A COA was entered into between the Department and Diversified on March 7, 2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216.At the time of this inspection, the Departmnet observed an unrestored dirt/gravel access road leading to the Dinunno 1 plugged well site. A mailbox was at the plugged well site's entrance, however, no erosion and sediment plans for plugging were observed to be present in the mailbox. The Department recommends an E and S plan be available on site during all stages of earth disturbance activity in accordance with 102.4b8.At the time of this inspection, the Department traveled to the plugged well's cooridnate GPS location and did not observe any fluid leaks or fluid dischages at the surface of the plugged well's approximate location. At the time of this inspection, the well site appeared to be exhibiting 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion and sedimentation issues observed, however, erosion and sediment control features (Compost Filter Sock) were observed to still be installed on site and what appears to be a graveled channel was observed on the edge of the well site. No production equipment appeared to be on site at the time of this inspection.Based on today's inspection, it appears that the well site and access road are not restored, therefore, violations are being issued for failure to comply with an COA of the Department (failure to restore the plugged well site by 12/20/2025 - 9 months from plugging).Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an Inspection App IT error.

properties.content:

Permit API: 117-21982
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-07-24
Comments: Wellhead painting on location, no other activity initially noted. Sitewide containment had been pulled up and rig mats were stacked. Many puddles were present on the pad; conductance readings in these puddles ranged from .7 to 1.4 mS/cm. Water was present in the area where the high conductance fluid had been noted during the frac; conductance reading was .98 mS/cm. I walked down the fill slope to the intercept trench and met Nick Shelman of Principal Enterprise. The intercept was nearly full of water and Nick was firing up the pump to move the water to the Baker tanks on the pad. Nick informed me that the pump was manned during the day and overnight if rain was expected. Conductivity of the water in the intercept was .55 mS/cm. The outlet to the sed trap had been filled in; water in the sed trap showed conductance of .35 mS/cm.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 2/01/2024
Comments: On February 1, 2024, inspection conducted at the Athena well pad in Washington Township, Westmoreland County. ESCGP approval was obtained on January 10, 2022 and expires on January 9, 2027. Present were Olympus Energy representative Laura Karosic, independent consultants Brad Latimer and Jeff Leary, and myself. Briefly present was Olympus Energy representative Jim Noon. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that was discovered while removing containment from the pad. The operator reports discovering at least 5 gallons of an oily material on the well pad. The following was observed:At the time of inspection, the Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The ERP, PPC plan, ESCGP approval letter, and E and S inspection logs were onsite (see photos 2-4). However, no E and S inspections beyond November 22, 2023 were available in the log onsite. The access road appeared to be stable with no evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The well pad was excavated at the time of inspection to install flow lines to the newly-drilled Utica wells onsite (see photos 6 and 14). A stained area of approximately 65 feet by 55 feet (according to measurements taken by the operator) was observed on the pad (see photos 7-10). Onsite consultants stated that they attempted to dig into the stained gravel in an attempt to gauge how far down the staining goes, but were unable. Ms. Karosic reported conductivity readings below 1,000 Microsiemens in the stained area. She also reported that the well pad drainages were closed-in upon discovery of the stained area. She informed the DEP that sampling will be conducted and remediation will be handled by Moody and Associates within the coming week, and additional information will be provided as additional discoveries are made in their investigation. The operator anticipates to conduct remediation in accordance with Act 2. Because it is unknown when the secondary containment failed, the DEP inquired on the timeline that it was on the pad. The aforementioned representatives informed the DEP that containment was first placed on the pad in late July of 2023 for drilling of the two Utica wells. Additional containment layers and rig mats were placed approximately six months ago for Completions, and the two Utica wells currently await to be fracked. GPU units onsite are equipped with raised secondary containment skids (see photo 13). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 11). The six additional wells onsite that appear to be in production were equipped with well tags, and did not appear to have any evidence of leaks or discharge on the ground around them at the time of inspection (see photo 15). All other containments onsite that appeared to contain regulated substances were placed in secondary containment. PCSM BMP's appeared to be constructed according to the plans onsite. The Department checked the downslope well pad drainages for any evidence of staining or impact from the newly discovered spill. No staining, distressed vegetation, or anything that would substantiate the occurrence of a recent spill was observed (see photos 5 and 18-25). Before departing from site, the DEP spoke with Olympus representative Jim Noon to inform him that the onsite E and S inspection log was incomplete, and that this has also been observed at another Olympus Pad. He stated that Olympus will conduct additional follow up with their EI's and provide them electronically for this site.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued for releasing this unknown oily substance to the surface of the well pad. An additional violation is being issued for threatening the WOTC, as the ground water depth appears to be shallow at approximately 15-200 centimeters in this area according to surveys conducted by the USDA.

Comments: This inspection has been conducted in response to an anonymous complaint submitted to the Department on July 29, 2020. These allegations have been verified in the field. A large crack exists on the eastern facing side of the tank. Fluid seems to have drained at a slow but steady rate from above the crack. Comments: On 06/03/2024, an incident inspection was conducted at the Zemba 1 well site following receipt of a spill report submitted by the operator on 05/31/2024 (CTS 381125). Penneco representatives on site. I called the operator on 06/03/2024 and they said that approximately 5 to 6 barrels were spilled on site and that the tank was cracked. The incident was discovered 05/31/2024 at 11:30 am and was reported to the Department on 05/31/2024 at 3:00 pm.Conductivity probe calibrated on 06/03/2024.The following was observed:The operator and well's information were posted on site, however the first three digits of the API were reading 126 instead of 125. I recommend that this is addressed. The tag on the well was displaying the last six digits of the API and not 125 (Photos 1, 2).Conductivity readings were taken at the site in the area that appeared to be impacted. A section of grass was dead and discolored near the tank (Photos 3-5). Readings were taken before and after calibration of the conductivity probe.Readings before calibration ranged from 25.4-852 uS/cm (Photos 6-9).Readings after calibration ranged from 227-1142 uS/cm (Photos 10-16).The tank was removed and additional readings were taken within the area with focus on the wet spots (Photos 17, 18). Readings were 20.5 uS/cm and 205 uS/cm (Photos 19, 20).The wellhead was in generally good condition with some corrosion (Photo 21).The Department requests the type of material released (brine or oil). The Department recommends that the Spill Policy is utilized due to a spill larger than 42 gallons. The Department also requests information on why the remediation was not started and/or the spill immediately addressed. Due to the observation of dead grass which is indicative of a fluid impact from the well site, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78.66(b), and 78.66(e) are being issued.

Readings were taken before and after calibration of the conductivity probe.Readings before calibration ranged from 25.4-852 uS/cm (Photos 6-9).Readings after calibration ranged from 227-1142 uS/cm (Photos 10-16).The tank was removed and additional readings were taken within the area with focus on the wet spots (Photos 17, 18). Readings were 20.5 uS/cm and 205 uS/cm (Photos 19, 20).The wellhead was in generally good condition with some corrosion (Photo 21).The Department requests the type of material released (brine or oil). The Department recommends that the Spill Policy is utilized due to a spill larger than 42 gallons. The Department also requests information on why the remediation was not started and/or the spill immediately addressed. Due to the observation of dead grass which is indicative of a fluid impact from the well site, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78.66(b), and 78.66(e) are being issued.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: Arrived onsite as a followup to inspection 3981577 from 5/20/25. It was about 47 F and raining. Equipment was being installed for flowback and future production.The sumps on the northern and southern side of the 5HC well cellar were installed. The sumps were accessible via a plastic pipe that extended about 1.5 feet above the surrounding ground. There was some fluid observed in the sumps but it could not be reached with a conductivity meter.The closest puddle to the sumps was approximately 15 to 20 feet north of the 5HC well. The conductivity of the puddle was 453 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). Additional conductivity readings were taken from water leaving the pad and entering the infiltration basins. Readings were taken at the main entry point to the basins, near the middle, and at the far end of the basins. The first basin checked was the more eastern of the two and the readings were 182.9, 173.3, and 109.4 uS/cm, respectively.
